question: Which continent provides more than half of world’s tin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asia produces more than half of the world's tin. Tin is a soft, malleable metal mainly used for tin-plating and in alloys such as bronze and solder. (टिन — एशिया महाद्वीप का प्रमुख उत्पाद)

 

• The largest tin-producing countries — China, Indonesia, Myanmar, and Malaysia — are all located in Asia; together with other Asian producers they contribute more than 50% of global tin output.

 

• The Southeast Asian "tin belt," stretching from Myanmar through Thailand and Malaysia to Indonesia, is historically one of the richest tin-producing regions in the world.

 

• Notable tin producers outside Asia include Peru, Bolivia and Brazil in South America and the Democratic Republic of Congo in Africa, but their combined share is much smaller than Asia's.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India also has tin reserves, mainly in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, though it is not a major producer globally.

 

• Tin is a key component of bronze (copper + tin) and is widely used in electronics for soldering.

 

NOTE

 

• Europe (Option 1): Europe has minor historic tin deposits (e.g., Cornwall in the UK) but is not a major global tin producer today.

 

• North Africa (Option 3): North Africa has negligible tin production and is not among the world's major tin-producing regions.

 

• Africa (Option 4): The Democratic Republic of Congo and a few other African nations produce tin, but Africa's overall share is far below Asia's.

question: Breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid and energy in lack of oxygen takes place in which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Human muscle cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid (with release of energy) in the absence of oxygen is called lactic acid fermentation / anaerobic respiration, and it occurs in human (and other animal) muscle cells during intense exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient. (अवायवीय श्वसन — मानव पेशी कोशिकाएं)

 

• This process regenerates NAD+ from NADH so glycolysis can keep producing a small amount of ATP even without oxygen.

 

• The lactic acid that accumulates in muscles is responsible for the fatigue/cramping felt after strenuous exercise.

 

• In contrast, yeast cells undergo alcoholic fermentation in the absence of oxygen, converting pyruvate into ethanol and carbon dioxide, not lactic acid — this is the standard textbook distinction between the two anaerobic pathways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aerobic respiration (with oxygen), which occurs mainly in the mitochondria, breaks pyruvate down completely into CO2 and water, releasing far more ATP than anaerobic respiration.

 

• Anaerobic (lactic acid) fermentation itself takes place in the cytoplasm, not inside the mitochondria.

 

NOTE

 

• Bacteria (Option 1): Certain bacteria (e.g., Lactobacillus, used in curd formation) do carry out lactic acid fermentation, but in the standard textbook contrast of anaerobic pathways, lactic acid formation is specifically identified with muscle cells while ethanol formation is identified with yeast.

 

• Yeast (Option 3): Yeast breaks down pyruvate into ethanol and CO2 (alcoholic fermentation), not lactic acid.

 

• Mitochondria (Option 4): Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle and electron transport chain), which requires oxygen; the anaerobic conversion to lactic acid happens in the cytoplasm.

question: Hari Prasad Chaurasia is associated with which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bansuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is one of India's most celebrated Hindustani classical musicians, renowned for playing the bansuri (Indian bamboo flute). (बांसुरी — भारतीय बांस की बांसुरी)

 

• He is widely credited with elevating the bansuri from a folk instrument to a prominent solo classical concert instrument, alongside instruments like the sitar and sarod.

 

• He is a recipient of major national honours, including the Padma Vibhushan, in recognition of his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

• He is also known for the musical duo "Shiv-Hari" with santoor player Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, and for composing music for several Hindi films.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute traditionally associated with Lord Krishna in Indian iconography.

 

• Other well-known bansuri players include Pandit Ronu Majumdar and Rakesh Chaurasia (Hariprasad Chaurasia's nephew and disciple).

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 1): A pair of hand drums, associated with maestros such as Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha, not Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

• Veena (Option 3): A plucked string instrument central to Carnatic music, associated with artists such as S. Balachander and Chitti Babu.

 

• Drum (Option 4): A generic percussion instrument; not the instrument Hariprasad Chaurasia is known for.

question: International Women’s Day is celebrated on?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8th march.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• International Women's Day is observed every year on 8th March worldwide, celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय महिला दिवस — 8 मार्च)

 

• It also serves as a call to action to accelerate progress toward women's equality.

 

• The day has its roots in early 20th-century labour movements in North America and Europe, and was first officially observed by the United Nations in 1975 (declared International Women's Year).

 

• The United Nations announces a specific theme for International Women's Day each year to focus global attention on a particular issue affecting women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• International Men's Day is observed on 19th November.

 

• The 2022 UN theme for International Women's Day was "Gender equality today for a sustainable tomorrow."

 

NOTE

 

• 12th July (Option 1): This date is actually observed as World Population Day, not Women's Day.

 

• 12th march (Option 2): No major international observance related to women is associated with this date.

 

• 8th July (Option 3): An incorrect distractor that swaps the day and month of the correct date; no major women-related observance falls on this date.

question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Maratha dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (1630–1680) was the founder of the Maratha Empire in western India, celebrated for his military genius, guerrilla warfare tactics (Ganimi Kava), and efficient administration. (छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज — मराठा साम्राज्य के संस्थापक)

 

• He was formally crowned Chhatrapati (sovereign ruler) at Raigad Fort in 1674.

 

• He established a strong navy and an efficient administrative system, including the Ashtapradhan (council of eight ministers), and championed the idea of Swarajya (self-rule).

 

• His successors, including his son Sambhaji and later the Peshwas, further expanded the Maratha Empire across large parts of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shivaji Maharaj's coronation in 1674 is considered a landmark event, marking the formal establishment of an independent Maratha kingdom.

 

• The Maratha Empire, at its peak in the 18th century under the Peshwas, extended over most of the Indian subcontinent.

 

NOTE

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan (Option 1): The last Hindu ruler of the Chauhan dynasty of Delhi/Ajmer, defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

 

• Man Singh (Option 2): A Rajput general and one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in Emperor Akbar's Mughal court.

 

• Porus (Option 4): An ancient Indian king who fought Alexander the Great at the Battle of the Hydaspes (326 BCE).

question: The book titled ‘The Ministry of Utmost Happiness’ has been written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017) is a novel written by Arundhati Roy, her second novel after her Booker Prize-winning debut "The God of Small Things" (1997).

 

• The novel was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize in 2017.

 

• Arundhati Roy is also widely known for her essays and activism on social, environmental, and political issues in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• "The God of Small Things" won the Booker Prize in 1997, making Arundhati Roy the first Indian woman to win the award.

 

• Both of Arundhati Roy's novels deal with themes of identity, marginalization, and social conflict in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Jia Pingwa (Option 1): A contemporary Chinese novelist, known for works such as "Ruined City" and "The Shaanxi Opera."

 

• Sunita Narain (Option 3): An Indian environmentalist and Director General of the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE), not the author of this novel.

 

• Dan Brown (Option 4): An American author known for thriller novels such as "The Da Vinci Code" and "Angels & Demons."

question: In September 2022 at Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX) in Bengaluru, ISRO and space agency of ______ facilitated signage of half a dozen MoUs between the startups of the two countries focusing on the space tech.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 7th Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX-2022) was held in Bengaluru, Karnataka, in September 2022, organized by Antrix Corporation (ISRO's commercial arm) along with industry partners.

 

• At BSX-2022, ISRO and the Australian Space Agency facilitated the signing of about half a dozen MoUs between Indian and Australian space start-ups, focusing on cooperation in space technology.

 

• This event reflected the growing India–Australia collaboration in the space sector under bilateral cooperation frameworks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bengaluru is often called India's "Space City" owing to the presence of ISRO headquarters and several major space-tech start-ups.

 

• India–Australia space cooperation has grown in recent years, including areas like satellite navigation, space situational awareness, and commercial space start-up partnerships.

 

NOTE

 

• France (Option 2): France (via CNES) collaborates with ISRO on various missions, but was not the partner agency in this specific BSX-2022 MoU-signing event.

 

• USA (Option 3): NASA collaborates with ISRO on missions such as NISAR, but was not the agency referenced in this specific event.

 

• Israel (Option 4): The Israel Space Agency partners with ISRO on select missions, but was not involved in this specific BSX-2022 MoU event.

question: In 1757, ______ led the Company’s army against Sirajuddaulah at Plassey.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Clive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757), Robert Clive led the forces of the British East India Company against Nawab Sirajuddaulah of Bengal. (प्लासी का युद्ध — रॉबर्ट क्लाइव)

 

• Clive's victory was aided by the betrayal of Mir Jafar, Sirajuddaulah's commander, who withheld his forces from the battle and was later installed as the puppet Nawab of Bengal by the British.

 

• This battle marked the beginning of British political control in India and laid the foundation for British colonial rule in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated Company control over Bengal, leading to the grant of Diwani (revenue collection rights) of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the Company in 1765.

 

• Robert Clive later served as the first Governor of the Bengal Presidency.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 1): A later Governor-General known for the Permanent Settlement of Bengal (1793) and the Cornwallis Code.

 

• Lord Minto (Option 2): A Governor-General associated with the Minto-Morley Reforms (Indian Councils Act, 1909).

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 3): The first Governor-General of Bengal (1773–1785), associated with the Regulating Act of 1773 and the Rohilla War.

question: Which among the following festivals is celebrated as the Telugu New Year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ugadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi is celebrated as the traditional New Year's Day by the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka (where it is called Yugadi). (उगादी — तेलुगु नव वर्ष)

 

• It usually falls in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April) as per the lunisolar calendar.

 

• The festival is marked by the preparation of "Ugadi Pachadi," a dish combining six different tastes — sweet, sour, salty, bitter, tangy, and spicy — symbolizing the varied experiences of life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra and Cheti Chand by the Sindhi community.

 

• Telugu literary works and calendars (panchangas) are traditionally released or read out on Ugadi.

 

NOTE

 

• Monpa (Option 1): Refers to an ethnic community/tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, not a New Year festival.

 

• Vishu (Option 3): The traditional New Year festival of Kerala, celebrated in mid-April.

 

• Dasara (Option 4): A major Hindu festival celebrating the victory of good over evil (Vijayadashami), celebrated grandly in Mysuru, Karnataka; it is not a New Year festival.

question: According to WHO, If a person’s BMI is below 18.5 he/she is classified as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Underweight.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the WHO's Body Mass Index (BMI) classification, a person with a BMI below 18.5 kg/m² is classified as "Underweight."

 

• BMI is calculated as weight (kg) divided by the square of height in metres: BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]².

 

• WHO's standard classification: below 18.5 = Underweight; 18.5–24.9 = Normal weight; 25–29.9 = Overweight; 30 and above = Obese.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• BMI is a simple screening tool and does not directly measure body fat percentage; factors like muscle mass can affect its accuracy for individuals.

 

• Being persistently underweight can be associated with nutritional deficiencies and a weakened immune system.

 

NOTE

 

• Mentally unfit (Option 1): BMI is a measure of body weight relative to height and has no connection to mental fitness.

 

• Blind (Option 3): Unrelated to BMI; blindness is a distinct medical condition unconnected to body weight measurement.

 

• Healthy (Option 4): A BMI in the 18.5–24.9 range is generally classified as healthy/normal weight, not a BMI below 18.5.

question: Which of the following pressure belt is known as the horse latitude?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sub - Tropical High Pressure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "horse latitudes" refer to the subtropical high-pressure belts located around 30°–35° North and South of the equator, where winds are calm and light due to descending, warm, dry air.

 

• The term is believed to derive from the historical practice of sailing ships becoming becalmed in these latitudes, sometimes forcing sailors to throw horses overboard to conserve water and supplies.

 

• These belts are associated with arid climates; many of the world's major deserts (e.g., the Sahara) lie near these latitudes due to the persistent descending, dry air.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The subtropical high-pressure belts also give rise to the trade winds (blowing towards the equator) and the westerlies (blowing towards the poles).

 

• The equatorial low-pressure belt (doldrums) lies between the two subtropical high-pressure belts.

 

NOTE

 

• Sub - Polar Low Pressure (Option 1): Located around 60°–65° latitude, associated with rising air and stormy weather, not the horse latitudes.

 

• Equatorial Low Pressure (Option 2): Also known as the doldrums, located near the equator, associated with rising warm, moist air and heavy rainfall.

 

• High Pressure (Option 4): Too generic a term; the horse latitude specifically refers to the subtropical high-pressure belt, not high pressure in general.

question: Who is the first Indian President to be born in Independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Droupadi Murmu (born 20 June 1958) became the 15th President of India in July 2022, and is the first Indian President to have been born after India's independence (15 August 1947). (द्रौपदी मुर्मू — स्वतंत्र भारत में जन्मी पहली राष्ट्रपति)

 

• She is also the first person from a tribal (Santhal) community, and only the second woman (after Pratibha Patil), to become President of India.

 

• Before becoming President, she served as the Governor of Jharkhand (2015–2021) and earlier held ministerial and legislative positions in Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Droupadi Murmu took oath as President of India on 25 July 2022.

 

• She succeeded Ram Nath Kovind as the 15th President of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Pratibha Patil (Option 1): India's first woman President (2007–2012), born in 1934, before independence.

 

• Ram Nath Kovind (Option 3): The 14th President of India (2017–2022), born in 1945, before independence.

 

• Pranab Mukherjee (Option 4): The 13th President of India (2012–2017), born in 1935, before independence.

question: Wages/day under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA is ______, w.e.f. 1st April, 2020, as per Economic Survey 2020-21.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs 202.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Economic Survey 2020-21, the average wage rate under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was revised to Rs 202 per day, with effect from 1st April 2020.

 

• MGNREGA, enacted in 2005, guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment per financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

 

• Wage rates under MGNREGA are revised annually for each state based on changes in the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Actual state-wise MGNREGA wage rates vary considerably — from lower amounts in some states to well above Rs 300 in states like Haryana; Rs 202 represents the cited national average/reference figure.

 

• MGNREGA is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rs 182 (Option 1): Not the figure cited in the Economic Survey 2020-21 for the wage rate effective 1 April 2020.

 

• Rs 412 (Option 2): Not a figure associated with the MGNREGA average wage rate.

 

• Rs 152 (Option 4): Not the figure cited in the Economic Survey 2020-21 for MGNREGA wages.

question: Sheetal wants to create financial statements for her business. Which among the following software should she use for the same?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spread sheet software.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spreadsheet software (such as Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets) is specifically designed for organizing, calculating, and analyzing numerical/tabular data — making it the appropriate tool for preparing financial statements like balance sheets and profit & loss statements.

 

• Spreadsheets offer built-in formulas, functions, formatting tools, and charting features that are essential for financial calculations and summaries.

 

• Spreadsheet applications also allow data to be easily updated, audited, and presented in structured rows and columns, which suits accounting needs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Popular spreadsheet software includes Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, and Apache OpenOffice Calc.

 

• Application software (like spreadsheets, word processors, and presentation tools) is designed for specific end-user tasks, unlike system software which manages the computer itself.

 

NOTE

 

• Multimedia software (Option 1): Used for creating or editing audio, video, and animation content, not financial data.

 

• Presentation software (Option 2): Used for creating slideshows (e.g., Microsoft PowerPoint) for presentations, not financial statements.

 

• System software (Option 3): Refers to operating systems and utility programs that manage computer hardware and resources, not for creating financial documents.

question: As on November 2022, who is the first citizen of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The President of India is often referred to as the "First Citizen of India," being the head of state and the highest constitutional authority in the country.

 

• Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25th July 2022, and as of November 2022 (the reference point in the question) she was serving as President, making her the First Citizen of India.

 

• As President, she is the ceremonial head of state, the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces, and holds constitutional powers such as summoning and dissolving Parliament sessions and giving assent to bills.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vice-President of India is often referred to as the "Second Citizen," and the Prime Minister as the "Third Citizen," in the informal order of precedence.

 

• Droupadi Murmu is the second woman President of India, after Pratibha Patil.

 

NOTE

 

• Amit Shah (Option 1): Union Home Minister of India as of November 2022, not the President.

 

• Narendra Modi (Option 3): Prime Minister of India (head of government), not the head of state/First Citizen.

 

• Sonia Gandhi (Option 4): Former President of the Indian National Congress party; she has held no constitutional office as President.

question: Which among the following corridors was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahakal Lok Corridor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Mahakal Lok Corridor (Shri Mahakaleshwar Temple corridor) in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, on 11th October 2022. (महाकाल लोक गलियारा — उज्जैन)

 

• The corridor is part of the Mahakaleshwar Temple redevelopment project, aimed at improving pilgrim facilities and showcasing scenes from Hindu mythology through murals and sculptures depicting the life of Lord Shiva.

 

• It significantly expanded the temple precinct and enhanced the overall pilgrim experience at one of India's twelve Jyotirlingas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi, a similar large-scale temple redevelopment project, was inaugurated earlier, in December 2021 — not October 2022.

 

• Such corridor projects aim to boost religious tourism infrastructure at major pilgrimage sites across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (Option 2): An industrial infrastructure development corridor project, unrelated to a temple inauguration in October 2022.

 

• Kashi Corridor (Option 3): The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor was inaugurated in December 2021, not October 2022.

 

• North East Economic Corridor (Option 4): Not a corridor inaugurated by PM Modi in October 2022 in this context.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "term – sports" is correct?
I. Eagle – Hockey
II. Penalty kick - Volleyball
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: "Eagle" is a scoring term used in golf, referring to a score of two strokes under par on a hole. It is not a hockey term.

 

• Statement II is incorrect: "Penalty kick" is a term used in football (soccer), awarded when a defending team commits a foul inside its own penalty area. It is not a volleyball term — volleyball uses terms like service, spike, block, and rally.

 

• Since both given statements pair the sports term with an incorrect sport, neither statement is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In hockey, terms such as "short corner," "long corner," "penalty stroke," and "bully" are commonly used.

 

• In golf, other scoring terms include "birdie" (one stroke under par), "bogey" (one stroke over par), and "par" (the expected number of strokes).

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement I itself (Eagle–Hockey) is a wrong pairing.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since neither pairing is factually correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement II (Penalty kick–Volleyball) is also a wrong pairing.

question: Which of the following combinations of tenors of Treasury bills issued by Government of India is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 91 days, 182 days, 364 days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term government securities issued by the Government of India (through the RBI) to meet short-term financial requirements.

 

• T-Bills are currently issued in three standard tenors: 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days.

 

• They are issued at a discount to their face value and redeemed at par upon maturity, so the investor's return comes from the difference between the issue price and the face value (no periodic/explicit interest is paid).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Treasury Bills are issued through a competitive bidding process (auctions) conducted by the RBI on behalf of the Government of India.

 

• Unlike T-Bills, government dated securities (G-Secs) are long-term instruments with maturities extending beyond one year and generally pay periodic coupon interest.

 

NOTE

 

• 82 days, 182 days, 345 days (Option 1): An incorrect combination that does not match the actual T-Bill tenors.

 

• 61 days, 145 days, 360 days (Option 3): An incorrect combination that does not match the actual T-Bill tenors.

 

• 91 days, 152 days, 356 days (Option 4): Only the first tenor (91 days) is correct; the other two figures do not match the actual T-Bill tenors.

question: Fourth edition of Khelo India Youth Games was hosted by which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2021 was hosted by Haryana, with Panchkula as the primary host city (the Games were actually held in June 2022 owing to a COVID-related postponement).

 

• Haryana topped the overall medal tally at the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.

 

• The Khelo India Youth Games is an annual multi-sport event for young athletes in India, launched in 2018 to promote a grassroots sports culture across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 3rd Khelo India Youth Games (2020) was hosted by Guwahati, Assam, in January 2020.

 

• The 5th Khelo India Youth Games (2022) was hosted by Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, held in early 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Hosted the 5th Khelo India Youth Games (2022) at Bhopal, not the 4th edition.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Has hosted various national/international sporting events, but not the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Hosted the 3rd Khelo India Youth Games (2020) at Guwahati, not the 4th edition.

question: _________is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendragiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahendragiri, located in Gajapati district, Odisha, at an elevation of about 1,501 metres, is the peak traditionally cited as the highest point of the Eastern Ghats in standard geography references used for competitive exams. (महेंद्रगिरि — पूर्वी घाट की सबसे ऊंची चोटी)

 

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of hills running along India's eastern coast, from Odisha through Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu, generally lower and more fragmented than the Western Ghats.

 

• (Note: some newer surveys identify Jindhagada Peak/Deomali, also in Odisha, at about 1,690 m, as an even higher point of the Eastern Ghats range, but Mahendragiri remains the conventionally accepted answer in the standard exam syllabus and among the choices typically given.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahendragiri is also of religious and historical significance, mentioned in ancient Indian texts and associated with Parashurama in mythology.

 

• The Eastern Ghats are rich in mineral resources and are drained by major rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri as they flow to the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanchenjunga (Option 1): The third-highest mountain peak in the world, located in the Himalayas on the India–Nepal border in Sikkim, not in the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Khasi (Option 2): Refers to the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, part of the northeastern hill ranges, not the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Anai Mudi (Option 3): The highest peak of the Western Ghats (and of Peninsular India), located in Kerala, not the Eastern Ghats.

question: Which of the following is mentioned in state list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Betting and gambling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Betting and gambling" is Entry 34 in the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, meaning state legislatures have exclusive power to legislate on this subject.

 

• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers between the Union and the States into three lists: the Union List (List I), the State List (List II), and the Concurrent List (List III).

 

• Railways, Post Office Savings Bank, and Inter-State Trade and Commerce are all subjects that fall under the Union List, since they require uniform national-level regulation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union List currently has 100 subjects, the State List has 61 subjects, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects (after various amendments).

 

• Other State List subjects include police, public health and sanitation, agriculture, and local government.

 

NOTE

 

• Railways (Option 2): Entry in the Union List; railways are a Union subject as part of national transportation infrastructure.

 

• Post office saving Bank (Option 3): Falls under the Union List (Posts and Telegraphs), as postal services are a central government function.

 

• Inter-state trade and commerce (Option 4): Falls under the Union List, since it requires nationwide, interstate regulatory uniformity.

question: Each orbit of International Space Station (ISS) takes ______ minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 90 – 93.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Space Station (ISS) orbits the Earth at an average altitude of about 400 km, completing one full orbit approximately every 90–93 minutes (roughly 92 minutes).

 

• This means the ISS completes about 15–16 orbits of the Earth per day, and its crew experiences a sunrise or sunset roughly every 45 minutes.

 

• The ISS travels at a speed of about 28,000 km/h (approximately 7.66 km/second) in order to maintain its orbit against Earth's gravity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISS is a joint project involving space agencies such as NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada).

 

• It has been continuously occupied by rotating crews of astronauts since November 2000.

 

NOTE

 

• 85 – 87 (Option 1): Slightly lower than the ISS's actual orbital period.

 

• 83 – 86 (Option 2): Too low; does not match the ISS's actual orbital period.

 

• 80 – 82 (Option 4): Too low; does not match the ISS's actual orbital period.

question: When the grains of sand are very fine and light, the wind can carry it over very long distances. When such sand is deposited in large areas, it is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is loess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loess refers to fine, wind-deposited (aeolian) silt or sand particles that accumulate over large areas, often forming fertile, unstratified deposits. (लोयस — पवन द्वारा जमा महीन मिट्टी)

 

• Loess deposits are typically yellowish in colour and are found in regions such as the Loess Plateau in China, parts of the Great Plains in the USA, and parts of Europe.

 

• These deposits are known for their high agricultural fertility, owing to their fine, mineral-rich particle composition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wind is a major agent of erosion and deposition in arid and semi-arid regions, forming features such as sand dunes, loess deposits, and ventifacts.

 

• The Loess Plateau in China is one of the largest loess deposits in the world and supports significant agricultural activity.

 

NOTE

 

• stacks (Option 1): Isolated rock pillars formed by coastal erosion; unrelated to wind-blown sand deposition.

 

• moraines (Option 3): Deposits of rock debris and sediment carried and deposited by glaciers, not by wind.

 

• mushroom (Option 4): Refers to "mushroom rocks," wind-eroded rock formations shaped by differential erosion from wind-blown sand — this describes an erosional landform, not a term for a deposited sand feature.

question: What is the full form of FTP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is File transfer protocol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol, a standard network protocol used to transfer computer files between a client and a server over a computer network, such as the Internet.

 

• FTP uses a client-server model and typically operates over TCP ports 20 (data transfer) and 21 (control/commands).

 

• It is commonly used for uploading and downloading files to and from web servers and remote systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Secure variants of FTP, such as FTPS and SFTP, add encryption to protect data during transfer.

 

• Other common internet protocols include HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) for web browsing and SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) for email.

 

NOTE

 

• File text paging (Option 1): Not a recognized or valid networking term.

 

• File transfer paging (Option 2): Not a recognized or valid networking term; an incorrect combination of words.

 

• File text protocol (Option 3): Not a recognized or valid networking term/protocol.

question: India’s National Air Sports Policy was released in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's National Air Sports Policy (NASP) 2022 was released/launched by the Union Minister of Civil Aviation, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in August 2022.

 

• The policy aims to make India one of the top air sports nations by 2030, promoting activities such as aeromodelling, ballooning, drone sports, gliding, powered air sports, and skydiving, among others.

 

• It seeks to simplify regulatory processes for organizing and participating in air sports and to encourage private investment in the sector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The policy was formulated by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in consultation with various air sports federations and stakeholders.

 

• It also proposes setting up an Air Sports Federation of India (ASFI) as the apex body to regulate and promote air sports in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• 2000 (Option 1): No National Air Sports Policy existed in India in this year.

 

• 2012 (Option 2): No National Air Sports Policy was released in this year.

 

• 2016 (Option 3): No National Air Sports Policy was released in this year; this may be confused with other aviation-related policies, such as the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016.
